result_text:
# Track 26 — Interactive Drill-Down Report UX

**Status: PROPOSAL — requires Aaradhya/Tisha sign-off before implementation.** This resolves the open coordination flag on pass/fail dashboard semantics (unresolved since the original report-template sprint) and follows the project's own Watkins et al. 2022 caution against bare threshold pass/fail framing for disparate impact.

## Resolution summary

Replace the binary verdict with a 3-tier progressive-disclosure structure. Tier 1 uses scanning-aid language only ("flagged for review," never "PASS/FAIL"). Tiers 2–3 exist so anyone who wants the underlying statistics or model evidence can get to them in two clicks, without those numbers cluttering the top-level view.

## Tier 1 — Top-level summary view

**Purpose:** orient the reader on where to look, not deliver a verdict.

**Layout:** single horizontal banner at the top of the report.
- Left: report title, run date, model/dataset identifier.
- Center: the scanning-aid statement, e.g. "**3 of 12 subgroups flagged for review**" — rendered as plain text, not a colored pass/fail badge. No green/red; if color is used at all, a single neutral accent (e.g. amber) marks "flagged," and unflagged subgroups get no color treatment.
- Right: "View methodology" link (opens a static panel explaining what "flagged" means and links to the NFR-003 threshold definitions and the lit-review note on why this isn't a compliance verdict).

**Default state:** expanded (it's the entry point). Below the banner, a table of all subgroups, one row each, collapsed by default:
- Subgroup name
- Flag status: "Flagged" / "Not flagged" / "Insufficient sample" (text label, not icon-only, per NFR-003 — insufficient-sample subgroups must never render as either flagged or unflagged)
- One-line metric preview (e.g. "selection rate ratio: 0.71")

No CI, p-value, or n at this tier — that's Tier 2. Row order: flagged subgroups first, then insufficient-sample, then not-flagged, each block alphabetical.

## Tier 2 — Subgroup-level detail view

**Trigger:** click/expand a row from Tier 1.

**Layout:** expands inline (accordion), not a modal or new page — keeps the reader anchored to Tier 1's context.

**Contents, in fixed order:**
1. Metric value with its definition (one sentence, e.g. what "selection rate ratio" means).
2. Confidence interval, plotted as a simple horizontal interval bar with the point estimate marked, plus the numeric CI bounds as text.
3. p-value, with the significance threshold used stated alongside it (not just a bare number).
4. n (sample size for this subgroup), with the insufficient_sample threshold shown next to it so the reader can see how close/far it is.
5. If `insufficient_sample` is true: a persistent inline notice — "Sample size below reliability threshold (n=X < Y); flag status not determined" — displayed above the metric value, not as a footnote.

**Default state:** collapsed. Only one subgroup expanded at a time by default (expanding a new one collapses the previous) to keep the page scannable; an "expand all" toggle is available for readers who want the full detail at once.

**Affordance to Tier 3:** for flagged subgroups only, a "View model evidence (SHAP)" link/button at the bottom of the expanded panel. Not shown for unflagged or insufficient-sample subgroups, since there's no evidence view to route to.

## Tier 3 — SHAP evidence view

**Trigger:** "View model evidence" from a flagged subgroup's Tier 2 panel.

**Layout:** separate expandable panel nested below the Tier 2 panel it was launched from (still inline, still anchored — not a page navigation), so the reader can collapse back to Tier 2 or Tier 1 without losing place.

**Contents:**
1. One-line framing: "Top features contributing to the flagged outcome for [subgroup]" — explicitly framed as model explanation, not proof of cause.
2. SHAP summary plot (feature importance, ranked) for the subgroup, top 10 features.
3. Short caption: SHAP values explain the model's behavior on this data; they don't establish legal causation or intent, and should be read alongside the Tier 2 statistics, not instead of them.

**Default state:** fully collapsed until explicitly requested — this is the most detailed tier and shouldn't load or render unless asked for, both for page performance and to keep it clearly opt-in.

## Cross-tier notes

- **Insufficient-sample handling is consistent top-to-bottom**: Tier 1 label, Tier 2 notice, and (since Tier 3 is unreachable for these) no SHAP link — a reader can never end up in a state that implies a determination was made when it wasn't.
- **No tier collapses the distinction between "flagged" and "fails."** Copy throughout uses "flagged for review," "requires review," or "outside expected range" — never "fail," "violation," or "non-compliant."
- **Sign-off dependency:** this UX resolves the coordination flag as a proposal only. Implementation should not proceed until Aaradhya and Tisha confirm the scanning-aid framing and tier boundaries, consistent with how this flag has been handled in prior rounds.
